unit.title: Python: lists and loops
unit.description: Lists, positions counted from 0, len, append, repeating code with for and range

cards.definition: The position of an item in a list, counted from 0: the first item is at index 0.
Counts from the end of a list: -1 is the last item, -2 the one before.
The name after for: it takes each value of the list in turn, one per turn of the loop.
cards.example: In for c in colors:, c holds one color at each turn.

cards.definition: Checks whether a value is in a list or a text, and gives True or False.
cards.example: "red" in colors is True if the list holds "red".

cards.definition: A variable increased by 1 at each turn, to count things; x += 1 is short for x = x + 1.
cards.example: count = 0, then count += 1 inside the loop.

cards.definition: Gives the whole numbers from 0 up to n, n not included: with 3, you get 0, 1 and 2.
cards.example: for i in range(3): runs 3 times.

exercises.explain: Indexes start at 0: fruits[0] is the first item, fruits[1] the second.
whyWrong: pear is at index 1: counting starts at 0.
kiwi is at index 2, the last one.
Index 0 exists: it is the first item.

exercises.explain: len() gives how many items the list holds. The last index is always len minus 1.
whyWrong: len counts the items from 1; only indexes start at 0.
There are three items, no more.
len gives a number, not the last item.

exercises.explain: A negative index counts from the end: -1 is the last item.
whyWrong: apple is the first item, at index 0.
pear is at index -2.
Negative indexes are allowed in Python.

exercises.prompt: What does the list contain after these lines?
exercises.explain: append() adds an item at the END of the list, and changes the list itself.
whyWrong: append adds at the end, not at the start.
append adds an item; it does not replace the list.
append changes the list: "hat" is now in it.

exercises.explain: for hands each item of the list to the loop variable in turn: first "red", then "blue".
whyWrong: The loop goes through every item, not just the first.
for gives the items themselves, not their positions.
c takes each value of the list in turn.

exercises.prompt: How many times is Hi printed?
exercises.explain: range(3) gives 0, 1 and 2: three values, so three turns. The stop value 3 is not included.
whyWrong: range(3) gives three values: 0, 1 and 2.
The stop value 3 is not included.
The indented line runs at every turn.

exercises.prompt: In ["a", "b", "c"], the item "c" is at index 3.
exercises.explain: Counting starts at 0: "a" is at 0, "b" at 1 and "c" at 2.
The loop adds each price to total: 0 + 5, then + 10, then + 15. A classic way to add up a list.
whyWrong: 15 is only the last price; the loop adds all three.
The prices are numbers, so + adds them.
total changes at every turn of the loop.

code.src:
total = 0
for price in [5, 10, 15]:
    total = total + price
print(total)

exercises.prompt: Build a line that adds "milk" at the end of the list shopping.
exercises.explain: shopping.append("milk") adds the item at the end. In JavaScript it would be push.

exercises.prompt: This script stops with an IndexError. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: The list has 3 items, at indexes 0, 1 and 2. Index 3 does not exist. The last item is names[2], or names[-1].
in checks whether a value is in the list and gives True or False.
whyWrong: "red" is in the list, so the answer is True.
in gives True or False, not a position.
It prints the answer of the test, not the item.

exercises.prompt: Build the first line of a loop that goes through every item of the list names.
exercises.explain: for name in names: then the indented lines run once per item.
